key_reasoning.reason: New ProjectModelPolicy abstraction (unrestricted / deny-all / whitelist modes) in model_availability_service is consumed by assistant agent, assistant engine builder, assistant service, conversation service, assistant factory (subagents), toolkit service (skill tools), core dependencies, exception formatting, and assistant routers/handlers including the hedged handler. Base L (shared utilities across 3 layers), bumped to XL because the change spans multiple agent/workflow paths.

Closest pattern is the existing ModelAvailabilityService whitelist checks, which this consolidates. Base M (refactor of an existing rule into one policy object). Bumped to L because the policy is an access-control gate: deny-all and whitelist semantics decide which models a project may run, and the fallback/substitution path must not silently widen access.

Diffstat reports 43 files changed (+2507/-387), including earlier MR commits and task-dir docs. The supplied list alone has 13 source files across agents/, core/, rest_api/ and service/ plus 20 test files, which is still XXL (16+).

Calibration note: the bundled L example (epmcdme-10401) scores Requirements Clarity L for open design gaps. Here the goal (one model rule for assistants, subagents and workflows) was defined, but three MR review rounds suggest gaps were settled during implementation, so M.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L to XL: affects multiple workflows/agents (assistants, built-in subagent clones, skill tools, workflow model selection)
Technical Risk bumped from M to L: touches authorization-like enforcement (project model whitelist / deny-all gate)
